entries.englishDefinition: Any one of numerous species of birds belonging to Turnix or Hemipodius and allied genera of the family Turnicidae. entries.englishDefinition: A groom's man, the best maThe two nights before a marriage among Muhammadans are called jAggA and mel. A small handful, as much as may be taken up with the thumb and fingers  a pinch of anything, as much as may be taken up with a thumb and finger  a snap of the fingers  a pendant sometimes attached to a nose ring:—chuTkI bajAuNA, To snap the fingers:—chuTkI bhar, A full handful:—chuTkI wichch kamm hoNA, To be performed (any work) quickly.
A lock of hair hanging from the top of the head, a cue or lock of hair worn behind.
To throw or shoot at a mark  to obtain an object without labor  PhuNDNA.

A tribe of agriculturists in the Multan and Muzaffargarh districtThey were originally Afghans who came to Multan from SivI and DhaDar for purposes of trade, and eventually settled at RaprI and the neighbourhood. In the confusion that followed the invasion of Tamerlane, Multan became independent of the throne of Delhi, and the inhabitants chose Sheikh YUsaf KureshI, head of the shrine of Sheikh Baha-ud-din, as governor. In 1445 D. Rai Sahra, chief of the LaNgAhs, whose daughter had been married to Sheikh Yusaf, introduced an armed band of his tribesmen into the city by night, seized Sheikh Yusaf and sent him to Delhi, and proclaimed himself king with the little Sultan Kutab-ud-DiThe dynasty terminated with the capture of Multan, after a siege of more than a year, by Shah Hasan AghUn, Governor of Sindh in 1526. For ten days the city was given up to plunder and massacre, and most of the LaNgAhs were slaiSultan Husain was made prisoner and died shortly after. The LaNgAh dynasty ruled Multan for eighty years, during which time the Belochis succeeded in establishing themselves along the Indus from Sitpur to KoT Karor. The LaNgAhs of Multan and Muzaffargarh are now very insignificant cultivators.

The birch (Betula Bhojputra, B. Jacquemontii, Nat. Ord. Betulaceæ) found abundantly in the Panjab HimalayIt grows to a higher elevation than most other trees, and may generally be seen occupying a tract above coniferous forestThe wood is almost valueless, and is only used for ploughs, small bridges at altitudes and in tracts where other trees are scarce. entries.englishDefinition: Tobacco (Nicotiana taba- cum, Nat. Ord. Solanaceæ.) The habit of smoking is universal in the East, but tobacco is not indigenous in AsiIt was introduced from England in the reign of the Emperor Akbar into IndiThe Sikhs are the only race whose religion prohibits tobacco. It was strongly prohibited by Guru Govind Singh. Amongst Moslems the plant is not harAm but makrUh, and the practice of smoking is "biddat" an act indifferent, one of those which have come into vogue after the death of Muhammad and are neither enjoined nor prohibited. Jahan- gir in the 14th year of his reign forbade smoking, persons who contravened the decree had their lips cut and several smokers in Lahore were paraded with blackened faces on donkeys, seated fronting the tail. Tobacco now has the widest range of cultivation of almost any economic plant and its use is universal. The species are tabacum, lattisima, fructicosa, Chinensis the source of the large Havannah cigars, rustica, the source of "Latakia" (Laodicea) Salo- nica (These alonica) and Turkey to- bacco, Persica, Shiraz tobacco, repandis the source of small Havan- nahs, quartivalves, multivalvis, nana are other specietabacum is cultivated in the Dekkhan, rustica, inthe north. The kinds of tobacco known in commerce are:—1. Kakkar, of which Kandhari, Lahori, Shikarpuri, Chilasi, Kalkatti are varie- ties, as well as those grown at other places in the Panjab. 2. The rumAnI whose colour is like the seed of a pomegranate is most esteemed. Inferior kinds are lAlRI, tam- brA, (garnets). Among rubies are reckoned the dUdI or tAnsalA, a smoky cairn- gorm, and the nariNgI or jacinth also called gulmidak, erroneously termed by English jewellers "Cinnamon ruby" The kinds called jafrAnI, jard or pokrAj are really pale and dark topazeAmongst rubies are also included sapphires "blue rubies," distinguished as kAbud, asmANI, surmaI (blue gray-colour of antimony).
